title: Local strict-perfect coefficient package
statement:
Work with sites small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, where $\mathcal O$ is a sheaf of commutative rings, with category of sheaves of modules $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an object $U$ use the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ and restriction of modules [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Put $\Lambda=\mathcal O_U$ in the following local notation. Let $Q\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be represented by a cochain complex $F^\bullet$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $F^r=0$ outside a finite interval. Here each $F^r$ is finite projective in the sheaf sense: it is a direct summand of a finite free sheaf $\Lambda^{\oplus n}$, whose sections are finite tuples of sections of $\Lambda$.

A strict-perfect coefficient package for this representation is the data, for each $r\in\mathbf Z$, of $N_r\in\mathbf N$ and $\Lambda$-linear sheaf maps
$$
F^r\xrightarrow{i_r}\Lambda^{\oplus N_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}F^r,
\qquad p_r\circ i_r=\operatorname{id}_{F^r}.
$$
Write $e_r=i_r\circ p_r$. The splitting relation gives
$$
e_r\circ e_r=e_r,\qquad p_r\circ e_r=p_r,\qquad e_r\circ i_r=i_r.
$$
These are degreewise splittings, with no requirement that $i_r$ and $p_r$ form chain maps into a preassigned free complex. For a cochain complex $K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules on $\mathcal C$, the local perfectness condition is that for every object $V$ of $\mathcal C$ there is a covering $\{V_\alpha\to V\}$ and, for each $\alpha$, a quasi-isomorphism $F_\alpha^\bullet\to K^\bullet|_{V_\alpha}$, where $F_\alpha^\bullet$ is bounded and each term is a direct summand of a finite free $\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}$-module, hence admits the package data above. An object $E\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ is perfect if it can be represented by such a $K^\bullet$. Bounds and ranks may depend on the covering object.

In the coefficient-ring case, let $\Lambda$ instead denote a commutative ring and let $Q\in D(\Lambda\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$ be perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Choose a bounded representative $F^\bullet$ of finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] $\Lambda$-modules. A global coefficient package consists of the same data with ordinary linear maps and $\Lambda^{\oplus N_r}$ the free module with its standard finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Its associated constant sheaf package on a site is obtained by sheafifying the constant presheaves termwise [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-sheafification], including the differentials, $i_r$ and $p_r$. The coefficient sheaf here is the constant ring sheaf $\underline\Lambda$; finite-product preservation [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] identifies $\underline{\Lambda^{\oplus N_r}}$ with $\underline\Lambda^{\oplus N_r}$.

lean.note: The recorded StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite is reused, not copied. The latest IsPerfectOnSmallRingedSite and SiteStrictPerfectCoefficientRepresentation interfaces fix coefficients at the site-object universe u+1. They cannot accept independent larger coefficient universe max r (t+1) on the small pro-etale site of object universe t+1 and morphism universe t. Generalize only the local-perfectness and representation wrappers to independent coefficient size. Original degreewise, ring-module and constant-sheaf constructions remain imported.
